newsitem.title: UK: British Land confident of second half.
newsitem.headline: British Land confident of second half.

text.p: Property group British Land, which on Tuesday reported increased half-year pretax profits of 34.2 pounds ($56.56) said on Tuesday it was confident of its outlook but the property market was competitive and variable.

"The prospects for the areas where we have invested continue to improve, with an added premium from our flexible methods of financing. I view the second half with confidence in a competitive though still variable property market," British Land's chairman John Ritblat said in a statement.
British Land confident of second half

British Land said the increase in pretax profits for the period was 81 percent, from 18.9 million pounds the previous year, when capital items were included. The group raised its interim dividend to 2.92 pence from 2.78 pence per share.

It said its activities were now wholly concentrated in the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland, adding that it had completed property sales totalling 100 million pounds since the end of March. These included the Atrium Twin Towers in Amsterdam and 90 Broad Street in New York.

During the same period British Land said it had completed purchases totalling 75 million pounds, including a department store in Birmingham and a retail warehouse in Stockton-on-Tees, both in England. Ritblat said the group was either financing or was negotiating extensions to 18 of its food superstores.

Ritblat said British Land's development programme was "proceeding well". The pretax profit figure was at the top end of analysts' forecasts and shares in the company had risen eight pence to 495.5 pence at 1220 GMT. ($1=.6047 Pound)
